questions.question: Which sensor gives the servo's measured position that the servo screen draws beside the commanded one? The choices are: the F4 encoder mounted on the servo output shaft; a sensor of its own that R11 selects (for example a magnetic angle sensor at the horn); or none in round 1.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:454 specifies no input and names the F4 encoder only as one that can sit on the servo output shaft. Until the sensor is named, P2 cannot tell whether this function needs a part, or which one. The screen takes the position as a pulse width in µs (shared/ui/include/servo_screen.h:67).

questions.question: If a sensor other than the F4 encoder gives the servo's measured position: what angular resolution must it have, in degrees, over what horn travel, in degrees?
questions.why: The tree gives no resolution or range for the measured position. The commanded side has 1 µs steps over 500 to 2500 µs (IOBoard.md:50), which fixes no angle. P2 cannot qualify an angle sensor without these. Not needed if the answer is the F4 encoder.

questions.question: When more than one rotation input reports (optical index, magnetic pickup, phase-wire clip, encoder, ESC telemetry), which one fills the BENCH rpm register and feeds the motor stall action? The choices are: a fixed priority order (state the order), or the one input a panel setting picks.
questions.why: The BENCH page has one rpm register with one valid bit (shared/link/include/link_pages.h:233; IOBoard.md:432). The stall action's rpm source is not stated either (IOBoard.md:434). Without the answer, P2 cannot say which inputs must run at the same time, or at what update rate.

questions.question: What is the highest shaft speed, in rpm, that the rotation inputs and the vibration path must follow?
questions.why: It sets each front end's highest input frequency. For the optical index, the encoder's index and the vibration fundamental that is rpm / 60. For the phase-wire clip, and for a pickup that reads the rotor's magnets, it is rpm / 60 × pole pairs, up to 21 pairs (MOTOR_POLES up to 42, docs/Link.md:159-160). 10,000 rpm is only Balance.md's example (docs/Balance.md:60-62). The BENCH register stops at 65,535 rpm.
questions.for_quantity: highest rpm the rotation inputs and the vibration path follow

questions.question: Down to which shaft speed, in rpm, must at least one rotation input keep reading, including the coast-down after a disarm?
questions.why: The ESC's speed stops 200 ms after the disarm (firmware/iomcu/src/outputs_hw.c:294-295; firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:663), so another input has to cover the coast-down (IOBoard.md:489). A phase-wire clip then reads back-EMF, and a variable-reluctance pickup's output, both of which fall with speed. Without the lowest speed, P2 cannot set those front ends' sensitivity or say which input covers the coast-down.
questions.for_quantity: lowest rpm the rotation inputs read

questions.question: What peak voltage, in V, must the phase-wire clip's input withstand: the 67.2 V of F15 plus what margin for switching overshoot and ringing on the motor phase?
questions.why: F15 (Research.md:543) bounds the pack, not the phase node, which rings above the pack at each switching edge. IOBoard.md:443 rates the clip at 67.2 V with no margin. The ESC pack switch's 67.2 V rating takes a margin that is asked for (IOBoard.md:189). Without the peak, P2 cannot qualify the clip's divider, clamp and comparator input.

questions.question: How does the phase-wire clip couple to the motor phase: galvanically, clipped onto the bare conductor, or without contact, through the wire's insulation?
questions.why: A galvanic clip needs a high-voltage divider and a clamp; a non-contact clip needs a high-impedance amplifier. The clip's conditioning is not stated (IOBoard.md:491). P2 cannot choose the front end's topology or qualify its parts without it.

questions.question: Is the phase-wire input galvanically isolated from the 3.3 V logic, and if so, to what isolation voltage, in V? Or is it referenced to the ground that the ESC pack's return shares at the star point?
questions.why: The isolation is not stated (IOBoard.md:491). The ESC pack's return reaches the star point by its own lead (IOBoard.md:547), so a divider referenced to that ground is possible. An isolator or an isolated supply would be a part R11 selects. Without the answer, P2 cannot tell whether that part is needed or qualify it.
questions.for_quantity: phase-wire clip isolation from the 3.3 V logic

questions.question: Which magnetic pickup does the input take, and does R11 select it or does the operator bring it? The choices are: a Hall-effect sensor with a digital output (state its supply voltage, in V), or a variable-reluctance coil with an AC output (state its peak voltage, in V).
questions.why: The pickup's type, supply and output are not stated (IOBoard.md:491). The owner's decision names only a magnetic rpm pickup (Research.md:65). A Hall sensor needs a supply, a pull-up and translation to 3.3 V; a coil needs a comparator with hysteresis and a clamp. P2 cannot choose between these front ends.
questions.for_quantity: magnetic pickup type, supply and output

questions.question: How many pulses per revolution does the magnetic pickup give: one per magnet added to the bell (state how many magnets), or one per rotor pole pair (MOTOR_POLES / 2, up to 21)?
questions.why: Whether the pickup's reading uses MOTOR_POLES is not stated (IOBoard.md:490). The highest rpm times this count sets the front end's highest input frequency, which P2 qualifies the front end against.

questions.question: Does R11 select the optical index sensor itself (a reflective sensor on a lead, aimed from below at the pen line on the motor bell), or only the IO board's front end for a sensor the operator brings? In the second case, at what supply voltage, in V, and with which output: open collector, push-pull or analogue?
questions.why: The optical index sensor's type, supply and output are not stated (IOBoard.md:491). The seeds for it, TLV3201 and TLV7011, are comparators only (Research.md:289). P2 cannot tell which parts this function takes.
questions.for_quantity: optical index sensor type, supply and output

questions.question: If R11 selects the optical index sensor: at what distance, in mm, does it read the pen line on the motor bell?
questions.why: A reflective sensor is specified for a working distance. The tree gives the mark and where it goes (docs/Balance.md:32-37) but no distance. P2 cannot qualify a sensor head without it.

questions.question: The accelerometer sits on the rig arm or the firewall. How is it built and bought: on a sensor board of its own that JLCPCB assembles (parts with LCSC numbers, under the IO board's sourcing rules), or as a part or module off the board, bought at Digi-Key (sourcing rule 1)?
questions.why: The accelerometer sits away from the IO board (docs/Balance.md:38-39, :45-46; IOBoard.md:493). Sourcing rule 1 (Research.md:134-139) covers a part on the IO board and a part off it, not a second assembled board. Without the answer, P2 cannot tell whether to search jlcparts or Digi-Key, or which stock gate applies.

questions.question: How long is the lead from the accelerometer on the rig arm or the firewall to the IO board, in m?
questions.why: The lead is not stated (IOBoard.md:493). Its capacitance loads the sensor's analogue output, and its length sets the noise it picks up. Together they decide whether the sensor end needs a buffer or a differential driver. P2 cannot qualify the output drive without the length.

questions.question: What full-scale acceleration, in g, must the vibration sensor measure without clipping?
questions.why: The tree states no range. P2 cannot qualify a sensor's measurement range without one.

questions.question: What is the smallest vibration amplitude at the rotation fundamental, in mg, that the balance measurement must resolve?
questions.why: It sets the sensor's allowed noise over the measurement bandwidth and, with the full scale, the dynamic range. The tree does not state it. P2 cannot qualify a sensor's noise density without it.

questions.question: What phase error, in degrees at the highest rpm, may delay variation add across the whole vibration chain: the accelerometer, the index pulse's front end and the converter together?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:449 says a constant delay cancels and its variation counts, but gives no limit. P2 cannot qualify the accelerometer's phase response or the index comparator's delay spread without a stated budget. R10 reports the converter's latency jitter for Q4 against the same figure.

questions.question: May the vibration sensor be a digital accelerometer with raw, unfused output and a known sampling instant (the IIS3DWB class, on SPI), or must it be analogue?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:447 requires an analogue sensor on the strength of docs/Balance.md:57-63. That page rules out a fused IMU streaming at 100 Hz, not a raw digital accelerometer. Research.md:289 makes the IIS3DWB a seed only if Q4 accepts a digital sensor. Q4 (Research.md:572) offers two analogue converters only and is decided after the research, so no digital part is ever qualified for it. Without the answer, P2 cannot set R11's candidate list.

questions.question: Are the encoder's 1 MHz (single-ended) and 5 MHz (RS-422) figures the count rate, in counts per second over A and B together, or the frequency of each of A and B, in Hz (a quarter of the count rate)?
questions.why: F4 asked for the highest count rate, and the answer gives MHz (Research.md:532). If 5 MHz is the frequency of each channel, the count rate is 20 million counts per second, four times the other reading. P2 cannot qualify the receivers, or R11 report the decode (IOBoard.md:446), without the unit.

questions.question: With the supply jumper at 12 V and the single-ended form selected, what is the highest signal voltage, in V, the single-ended input takes: 5 V, or the 12 V of an encoder whose push-pull outputs swing to its supply (HTL, high-threshold logic)?
questions.why: F4 sets the single-ended form at 5 V, and a separate jumper sets the supply to 5 V or 12 V (Research.md:532). An encoder on 12 V can output 12 V. P2 cannot qualify the input's voltage rating, or its translation to 3.3 V (IOBoard.md:105), without it.
